crossStoryFindings: The epic still has a split-brain around what counts as a process's 'current sources': read models, checkpoint planning, and rebuild/rehydrate use the active-source resolver, but refresh targeting and informed-work provenance still trust raw `currentMaterialRefs.sourceAttachmentIds`.

Soft detach and process-scope shadowing are therefore only consistently enforced on some runtime paths; other paths can still treat detached or shadowed source ids as current even after the UI and main process surfaces have switched to the resolved active-source view.
architectureFindings: The tech design makes Fastify-side active-source resolution the canonical shadowing rule for process current sources and environment planning, but `RuntimeSourceHydrationExecutor` and `SourceProvenanceService.recordInformedWorkForCurrentSources` bypass that seam.

The published provenance contract advertises `currentAttachmentVisibility: redacted`, but the runtime has no non-test producer for `access_revoked`/degraded provenance rows, so part of the API contract is still unattached to real execution behavior.
epicCoverageAssessment: The epic gate passed: `corepack pnpm run verify-all` completed successfully on May 4, 2026.

Automated coverage exercises attach/update/read flows, detach-aware rehydrate/rebuild planning, and degraded provenance rendering, but it does not cover shadowed-source refresh or informed-work provenance recording.

The `verify-all` e2e leg is still scaffold-only (`SKIP: test:e2e scaffolded in Story 0; no executable suite yet`), so there is no browser-level proof of the full attachment/refresh/provenance journey.
productionPathFindings: Source refresh is a real production path, but it currently rebuilds its working set from raw `currentMaterialRefs` instead of the active-source resolver the rest of the environment runtime uses.
The `redacted` provenance visibility mode is currently contract-only: the renderer understands it, but no production code produces an `access_revoked` degraded provenance record.

blockingFindings.title: Refresh planning bypasses active-source resolution and can rehydrate detached or shadowed-out sources
blockingFindings.evidence: `RuntimeSourceHydrationExecutor.refreshRecoverableSource()` resolves the target process from raw `currentMaterialRefs.sourceAttachmentIds` and then feeds those raw refs straight into `planHydrationWorkingSet()` (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-refresh.service.ts:92-159,223-320`). The epic's authoritative environment path first runs `resolveActiveProcessSourceAttachments()` to exclude detached rows and apply process-scope shadowing before planning (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts:1269-1289`, `apps/platform/server/services/processes/active-process-sources.ts:13-62`). Because detach only stamps `detachedAt` and never rewrites durable current refs (`convex/sourceAttachments.ts:279-317`), and project-shell refresh target counts are also derived from raw refs (`apps/platform/server/services/projects/readers/source-section.reader.ts:36-49`), refresh can still target or include sources that the active-source model has already removed from current use.

blockingFindings.title: Informed-work provenance ignores shadowing and can record duplicate or wrong-scope source relationships
blockingFindings.evidence: Process-scoped attach appends the new source id into `currentSourceAttachmentIds` without replacing the existing project-scoped id (`convex/sourceAttachments.ts:148-158,442-463`). The active-source resolver then hides the project-scoped row and shows only the process-scoped sibling for that process (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/active-process-sources.ts:42-59`), and the environment runtime uses that resolved set for current materials/checkpoint planning (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts:744-760,1269-1289`). `recordInformedWorkForCurrentSources()` does not use the resolver; it iterates raw `currentMaterialRefs.sourceAttachmentIds` and records provenance for every stored id (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts:36-75`). `buildSourceProvenanceEntry()` then exposes the recorded attachment's current scope/access/hydration verbatim (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts:174-199`), so a process can show one process-scoped current source in `materials.currentSources` while provenance records the shadowed project-scoped source as having informed the work, or records both rows for the same effective source.

blockingFindings.title: The shipped runtime cannot produce the required redacted provenance state
blockingFindings.evidence: `buildSourceProvenanceEntry()` can emit `currentAttachmentVisibility: 'redacted'` only when a stored record already carries `degradationReason === 'access_revoked'` (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts:202-228`). The only production write path, `createProvenanceRecord()`, always persists `entryStatus: 'ready'` and `degradationReason: null` (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts:153-171`), and a repo-wide search across non-test code finds no other writer for `access_revoked` or degraded provenance rows. That leaves the published redacted branch as a contract/test seam rather than real runtime behavior.
